newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere and Dasa alliance said "irreversible".
newsitem.headline: Lagardere and Dasa alliance said "irreversible".

text.p: Recent co-operation deals between Lagardere and Germany's Daimler Benz Aerospace (Dasa) in the space industry and missiles are "irreversible", whether or not Thomson-CSF's privatisation goes ahead, Matra Defense Espace chairman Noel Forgeard said in a newspaper interview.
"We are in an industrial logic. Partners are bound by their agreements, with or without Thomson," he told the business daily La Tribune.
In the space industry, this alliance will consist of a joint-venture company bringing together Dasa and Matra Marconi Space (MMS), a jointly owned unit of Lagardere and Britain's GEC.
In missiles, it will link Dasa subsidiary LFK to Matra BAe Dynamics, which is a 50-50 subsidiary of Lagardere and British Aerospace, he said.

"French interests will be preserved" in the new European units, Forgeard said, since Lagardere controls MMS, which will have "majority economic rights" in the new space unit probably to be named Matra Marconi Dasa.
Forgeard expects MMS chairman Armand Carlier to be chairman of the future firm, with Dasa chairman Manfred Bischoff to be head of the supervisory board.
In missiles, Matra BAe Dynamics may increase its stake in LFK to 49 percent from 30 percent in the next three years, Forgeard said.

The privatisation of Thomson-CSF is key to European defence industry restructuring to face U.S. competition in Forgeard's eyes, no matter the political outcome of Sunday's second round of parliamentary election, the paper said.

The privatisation of Thomson-CSF has been put on hold until the outcome of the election. The Socialists, who scored an upset victory in the first round of the legislative vote, have pledged to put privatisations on hold.
